recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. I have used their teas and tinctures on an almost daily basis for years now. Kyle is a great friend of InnerVerse and has appeared on the channel more times than I can count. These products work, not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

recFdBmTf1pJJOP6S.Body: LotusWei provides amazing and transformative plant essence elixirs, using one of nature's most gentle and beautiful elements: the flowers themselves. Led by founder Katie Hess, LotusWei supports customers with diverse products that operate on homeopathic principles and energetic resonances. I use LotusWei Elixirs to give me an edge with psychic & energetic sensitivity, discernment, and life force coherence. In other words, LotusWei Elixirs help me be a better podcaster and Biofield Tuner. Benefits accumulate over long term use!

recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Body: Clive de Carle has spent decades researching high-quality natural health essentials, from magnesium and fulvic minerals to iodine, selenium, and vegan-sourced vitamin D. His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.
recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Name: Clive de Carle

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Bio: Gabriel, known on air as Slick Dissident, co-hosts InnerVerse's Vibe Rant show and is a longtime recurring guest on the podcast. He teaches occult symbolism and tarot on his YouTube channel, ranging across the Major Arcana, the esoteric Enneagram, mythology and archetype, mystic linguistics, and the symbolism hidden in popular film. He is best known for Tarot-tories, his own system mapping the 22 Major Arcana and zodiac archetypes onto the geography of the United States.
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Name: Gabe (Slick Dissident)
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Role: Co-host of Vibe Rant; teacher of occult symbolism & tarot

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Release Work and Dropping Self Identification", "body": "S.B. Alger described the release technique he learned from his coach, traced it to Lester Levinson, and compared it with Anthony de Mello's book Awareness. He argued that the goal of his practice was imperturbability and that saying \"I am angry\" builds a box around a person, while noticing a feeling of anger loosens it. Later he walked through the method: place the emotion on a scale running from apathy to peace, welcome it, find the underlying want for approval, control or security, then ask whether it can be let go and answer honestly, even when the answer is no."}, {"title": "Naming and Combining Healing Modalities", "body": "Chance Garton explained that calling his work sound healing made people picture singing bowls in a yoga studio, when he found it more surgical and precise, and that he hesitated to call it Biofield Tuning because he was not certified through Eileen Day McKusick's program. He described a sacral chakra moving from numb, to painful, to pleasurable as energy rises, a ladder he compared with the scale of emotion. S.B. Alger said the two approaches probably naturally went together and imagined a group session pairing Chance's sound healing with his own spoken group release."}, {"title": "Solfeggio Numbers and Coherent Sound", "body": "Answering a question from a participant about finding personal frequencies, Chance Garton said he valued coherent vibration, meaning peaks and troughs balanced throughout. He explained that the Solfeggio tones fell into groups of one, seven and four, two, five and eight, and three, six and nine, which kept reducing back to three, six and nine without fractions or zeros. He said he did not put stock in claims that a single frequency would liberate anyone. Others traded stories about numbers that kept recurring in their lives, and the talk turned to 42 and the Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy."}, {"title": "Owls, Trees, and Lessons from Nature", "body": "Gordan Hamil told how the owls he had been spending time with watched a rattlesnake approaching their nest and never let it out of their sight, yet did not act because they knew it could not reach the young, which he called the biggest thing he had learned from the owls. Other participants said nature wastes no energy on preventative measures and described recharging beside a tree. Gordy also described an evening walk with his wife past a bush with hot dogs stuck in it, followed by owls and moving lights in the sky, which he captured on video, stressing that no claims were being made about what they were."}, {"title": "Gematria, Root Words, and Symbolic Patterns", "body": "One participant presented a graphic arguing that Senator Frank Church holding up the heart attack gun at the 1975 hearing echoed Perseus and Medusa, reading Church as Circe and claiming the word aloft matched Medusa in gematria. Later a caller argued that the tet, a circle with an X, was a root behind words and symbols for pillars, columns and the blue beam, and tied it to the tree of life, torsion and a coming polarity shift. Someone on the call linked these ideas to Ken Wheeler's work on magnetism."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Weaving Spiders co-conspirator S.B. Alger joins Vibe Rant! As a multidisciplinary artist, S.B. creates music, sculpture, paintings and more, teaches guitar and singing, and is a certified Release Coach. Hanging with S.B. is always good for deep thoughts and big laughs!
